slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to analyze how physician-to-physician versus physician-to-patient telehealth affects clinical outcomes and system utilization, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective when providing specialist access to physicians than direct access to patients.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare the health outcomes and costs of physician-physician versus physician-patient telehealth and Poison Control Center consultations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 100 simulation runs (1,000 patients, 100 physicians, 10 toxicologists) across various scenarios, measuring health improvement, hospital admissions, and cost per patient.
card.limitation: Uses simulated data and an incomplete model that assumes perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and no medical errors.

slides.title: Face versus Body Tracking for Human-Robot Interaction: An Egocentric Dataset
slides.highlight: This work introduces a custom dataset and evaluates face versus body tracking to reduce identity switches in social robots, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A new egocentric HRI dataset and evaluation showing body tracking with ReID outperforms face tracking.
card.key_idea: Systematic comparison of face vs. body tracking using extended temporal memory and appearance ReID to mitigate identity switches in close-quarter social robot interactions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a custom 20-sequence Furhat robot dataset using HOTA, IDF1, and IDSW metrics; optimized body tracking reduced IDSW by 49%.
card.limitation: Small dataset (20 sequences) from a single indoor environment; offline evaluation ignores real-time compute constraints and robot ego-motion.

slides.title: MASS: Deep Research for Social Sciences with Memory-Augmented Social Simulation
slides.tldr: MEMORY-AUGMENTED SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR LLM RESEARCH
slides.highlight: This work introduces MASS, a paradigm using realistic social simulations and memory mechanisms to improve the creativity and empirical grounding of LLM-generated social science research, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: MASS enhances social science research agents by using realistic social simulations to generate original empirical data.
card.key_idea: Integrates dynamic goal-path planning with social norm restraints, a 300K-entry multi-disciplinary behavior dataset for cold-start, and an Ebbinghaus-inspired structured forgetting mechanism for authentic agent simulations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DeepResearch Bench; showed 6.81% overall quality improvement over foundation LLMs and 17.19% gain in Insight over strong baselines.
card.limitation: High computational costs for large-scale simulations and potential for hallucinations in both text generation and agent decision-making.

slides.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Memory-as-a-Layer adapter to capture dialogue history and emotional context, supporting HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception of team states.

card.one_liner: MAL adds test-time neural memory to LALMs to capture dialogue context for conversational speech emotion recognition.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play Memory-as-a-Layer (MAL) adapter using Titans-style neural memory, integrated via additive residual updates and a two-stage LoRA-then-MAL training schedule.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, and MultiDialog using Qwen2-Audio, Audio Flamingo 3, and Ultravox-v0.4; showed consistent improvements in WA, UA, and WF1.
card.limitation: Broader coverage across more backbone-dataset combinations and comparisons against other memory architectures are still needed.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA UNCERTAINTY-GUIDED LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework enhances proactive robot assistance in household environments by combining Markov models with LLM reasoning to handle noisy conditions. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight framework combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered when prediction confidence falls below a threshold.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new noisy dataset, HOMER-Noise, against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using F1-scores; results show competitive accuracy and superior robustness to noise.
card.limitation: Inference latency is significantly higher than baselines due to external LLM API calls.

slides.title: Vietnam's Vingroup Unveils Two Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: Vingroup has introduced a guide bot and a factory bot, providing examples of humanoid applications relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: JAKA Pi Compact Humanoid for Labs, Schools, and Offices
slides.highlight: The introduction of a compact humanoid targeting labs and schools is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: IRAF: Interference-Resilient Adaptive Fusion for Noise-Robust End-to-End Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This work introduces IRAF to handle interfering speakers in full-duplex systems, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling during real-time human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: IRAF improves end-to-end full-duplex dialogue systems by gating user audio to resist interfering-speaker noise.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module predicts a frame-level reliability gate using target-speaker and user audio embeddings to rescale user representations before fusion with agent text embeddings.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MS-MARCO and InstructS2S-200K using BLEU, sBERT, and turn-taking metrics; IRAF outperformed CleanBase and NoisyAug baselines under interference.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.tldr: SOCIALLY-AWARE MOTION CONTROL FOR HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores how integrating social-aware motion control and psycho-cognitive perspectives into robot behavior improves social acceptability and human comfort. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for generating socially-aware robot motions that balance physical safety, task efficiency, and human acceptability.
card.key_idea: An MPC-based control architecture using velocity and interaction distance parameters to generate four distinct socially-informed behaviors while ensuring collision avoidance via separating-plane optimization.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-expert participants using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.
